list.title: The Saturn 3×3, written chronologically
list.desc: The 3×3 of Saturn carrying your name or the Basmala, in the archangels' frame. Write the cells in the order of their numbers, 1 to 9 as the book's fill runs, and draw the rules from the top-right corner for fire.
how: Draw the four horizontal rules, then the verticals, starting at the top-right corner (fire); start at another corner for air, water or earth.
Fill the cells in the order of their numbers — the first, then the second, and so on — not scattered: the course holds this raises its potency.
Write the name above and its value below; the four archangels go on the four sides.

list.title: The seven seals — the Greatest Name in a row

list.title: The hollow square with a name at its heart

list.title: The ḥurūf talisman of jīm
list.desc: Jīm spelt in full is 53; the 3×3 runs 49–57 with jīm itself in the centre and closes on 159. Round it jīm is written 53 times and Allah round that 66 times — the same figure the book prints on p.88 for the mansion al-Thurayyā.
how: Take the letter at its spelled value: جيم = 3 + 10 + 40 = 53.
Build the 3×3 with 53 in the centre: 52 57 50 / 51 53 55 / 56 49 54. Every line is 159.
Write the letter jīm itself in the centre in place of 53.
Round the square write jīm 53 times, and Allah round that 66 times.
Keep the intention open — the course warns against aiming it at one named person.

list.title: The Basmala cross — the seal of Solomon

Set it in a square: Jibrāʾīl on the right, Mīkāʾīl on the left, Isrāfīl above, ʿAzrāʾīl below.
Write the caliphs in the corners: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar above, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī below.
Write al-Shādhilī's name split, “al-” on one side and “Shādhilī” on another.
Optionally ring in maraja l-baḥrayni yaltaqiyān, baynahumā barzakhun lā yabghiyān with the openings.

list.desc: For the third mansion, al-Thurayyā, whose letter is jīm: made in its exaltation and carried, for access to the great and to gain one's object from them (p.88). A 3×3 of 49–57 round jīm, ringed by jīm and by Allah, under a hooded triangle of the same bands.
how: The square is jīm's own: 53 in the centre written as the letter, the cells 49–57 round it, every line 159 (the same construction as Durūs lesson 10).
Round it write “bismillāh” over and over, then a band of jīm, then Allah all round outside.
Above, the hood: a band of jīm between two rules, “bismillāh” along its top and Allah along its sides.
The book: made during the mansion's exaltation, and carried.
notes: Read cell by cell from the facsimile (the fives are written in the Maghribī way, like an 8): ٥٢ ٥٧ ٥٠ / ٥١ ج ٥٥ / ٥٦ ٤٩ ٥٤ — exactly 49–57 on the Lo Shu with jīm (53) in the centre; every line 159.
The rings read: an inner ring of بسم الله (seen as “ـسم … الله” in turn), a band of the letter ج, and an outer ring of الله.
Correction: the engine had attached this figure to the paragraph on al-Buṭayn (p.87); it belongs to al-Thurayyā on p.88, whose letter is jīm — which the rings confirm.

how: After the greater ablution, facing the qibla, write Āyat al-Kursī round the outermost circle; the Kufic letters in the second; the Names in the third.
In the fifth, Fard, Ḥayy, Qayyūm, Ḥakam, ʿAdl, Quddūs; in the sixth, the āya suited to your purpose.
At the centre the fourfold of that āya: its value less 30, divided by 4, the quotient in the first cell and one more in each; a remainder of 3, 2 or 1 lifts the 5th, 9th or 13th cell (p.1353).
Write it twice: carry one, soak the other and drink of it for nineteen days, reciting after every obligatory prayer.
